title: Latency fingerprinting and kernel-sensitivity index: measurement and runbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This page documents the Latency Fingerprinting methodology and the Kernel-Sensitivity Index (KSI) used by the serving runtime team to:
- Quantify per-kernel impact on P50/P95/P99 for representative text-generation workloads.
- Rank kernels by sensitivity so scheduling and preemption policies can be tuned without risking regressions.
- Provide a reproducible investigation runbook for tail-latency incidents attributed to kernel scheduling or kernel-level regressions.

Audience
--------
Primary: runtime engineers, SREs, performance QA, and release engineers. Secondary: product managers and infra owners who need a traceable cost/latency signal when evaluating kernel rollouts or quantization changes.

Why this matters
-----------------
We observe intermittent tail spikes that correlate with kernel version rollouts and heterogeneous job mixes. High-level SLOs are: P95 < 250ms, P99 < 800ms for short-sequence interactive routes; P50 < 30ms for control-plane fast-paths. Without a per-kernel sensitivity metric, rollouts rely on opaque aggregate telemetry and longer canary windows. KSI accelerates detection and points to a minimal remediation surface.

Definitions
-----------
- Latency fingerprint: a compact profile (histogram summary + contextual tags) describing how a specific workload shape (sequence length distribution, prompt tokenization class, decoding mode) maps to the latency curve observed on a given kernel build.
- Kernel-Sensitivity Index (KSI): a scalar in [-1.0, +1.0] representing the normalized change in tail latency attributable to a kernel compared with a baseline kernel. Positive KSI means the kernel increases latency.
- Workload shape: a tuple of {model_variant, avg_sequence_length, decoding_mode, batch_size_distribution}.

Measurement approach (high level)
--------------------------------
1) Select representative workload shapes from the operational workload catalog (see runtime-sandboxing lab manual). Each shape must include a seed prompt set (N=512) sampled from production anonymized traffic.
2) Run A/B microbenchmarks with deterministic seeds: baseline kernel (K0) vs candidate kernel (K1). Use traffic replay harness with request timing jitter to reflect production concurrency.
3) Collect per-request timing, kernel-name tag, compile flags, GPU occupancy, kernel queue depth, and full trace ids.
4) Compute the latency fingerprint (histogram quantiles plus conditional breakdowns) and the KSI per-shape.
5) Validate significance with bootstrap sampling (95% CI).

Detailed measurement protocol
-----------------------------
Prerequisites:
- Access to performance lab fleet with matching GPU family and driver version.
- Canary traffic replay harness (repo: infra/rl-replay) checked out at commit referenced in related_pages.
- Profiling agent v2.3+ installed (service: runtime-profiler).

Commands (example)
1) Install profiling agent and start harness:

$ git clone https://repo.internal/redwood/infra/rl-replay.git
$ cd rl-replay && ./setup.sh --gpu-family ampere --driver 555.40
$ ./replay --prompts seed_prompts_512.json --concurrency 128 --pacing jittered --profile --out /tmp/replay-output.json

2) Run candidate vs baseline pair with pinned kernel metadata:

$ ./replay --kernel-tag K0 --prompts seed_prompts_512.json --run-id baseline-2026-02-01 --profile --out baseline.json
$ ./replay --kernel-tag K1 --prompts seed_prompts_512.json --run-id candidate-2026-02-01 --profile --out candidate.json

3) Compute latency fingerprint and KSI (python tool):

$ pytools/latency_fingerprint/compute_ksi.py --baseline baseline.json --candidate candidate.json --out ksi_report.json

What the KSI output looks like
----------------------------
- ksi_report.json (example fields, abbreviated):
  - work_shape: "gpt-7b,avg_seq=64,topk=40"
  - ksi_value: "0.23"
  - p95_baseline: "312ms"
  - p95_candidate: "384ms"
  - p99_baseline: "820ms"
  - p99_candidate: "1102ms"
  - bootstrap_ci: "[0.18, 0.29]"
  - significant: "true"

Interpreting KSI
----------------
- KSI > +0.1: kernel is considered high-risk for the shape (investigate and block wide rollouts).
- +0.02 <= KSI <= +0.1: caution — prefer canary gating and extended sampling windows.
- -0.02 <= KSI <= +0.02: neutral — no action required beyond normal canary.
- KSI < -0.02: improvement — note in release notes and consider prioritized rollout.

Kernel-sensitivity matrix (example ASCII table)
------------------------------------------------
Each row is a workload shape; each column is a kernel candidate. Values are KSI (rounded).

| workload \t| kernel_K0 \t| kernel_K1 \t| kernel_K2 \t|
| short-chat \t| 0.00 \t| 0.23 \t| -0.04 \t|
| long-summarize \t| 0.00 \t| 0.07 \t| 0.12 \t|
| embeddings-batch \t| 0.00 \t| -0.02 \t| 0.01 \t|

This matrix is stored in the performance dashboard under: dashboards/ksi/matrix-latest (grafana).

Runbook: Investigate a kernel-attributed tail-latency incident
-------------------------------------------------------------
If an alert fires that correlates to a kernel rollout (alert name: kernel-sensitivity-p99-spike):
1) Triage: capture alert context, affected routes, and kernel-tag from the release event.
   - Owner: oncall-runtime (pager duty: runtime-team)
   - Initial data: timeframe, route(s), kernel-tag, % of traffic using kernel-tag.
2) Pull latency fingerprints for the top 3 affected shapes from the last 24h (dashboard query).
3) Run a quick A/B with the exact baseline and candidate on a staging replica using the seed prompts for the affected routes (10 minutes).
4) If KSI > +0.1 and bootstrap CI excludes 0: escalate to Kernel Rollout WG and block rollout. Create an issue: infra/kernel-rollout-blocker with the KSI report attached.
5) If KSI in (+0.02, +0.1): set temporary rate limit on the candidate kernel in the scheduler (see command below) and increase sampling to 4x for next 4 hours.
6) If neutral: continue monitoring and annotate release notes with the verification run id.
7) Record mitigations and postmortem if incident SLI impact exceeds threshold (sla-impact > 1 hour or customer-facing SLO breaches).

Commands to throttle candidate kernel in scheduler (example)
----------------------------------------------------------
- CLI (schedulerctl) to reduce slot weight for kernel-tag K1:

$ schedulerctl set-weight --kernel K1 --weight 0.2 --reason "ksi-quick-mitigation-2026-02-01"

- Revert:
$ schedulerctl set-weight --kernel K1 --weight 1.0 --reason "revert-ksi-mitigation"

Telemetry and observability contract
-----------------------------------
Every replay and production request must carry these trace tags:
- runtime.kernel_tag
- runtime.kernel_build_id
- runtime.kernel_variant (e.g., fp16-quant, int8-sym)
- runtime.kv_hit (true|false)
- runtime.queue_depth (integer)

Dashboards and alerts to check
-----------------------------
- dashboards/ksi/summary: KSI trend per kernel and workload shape.
- dashboards/latency/route-breakdown: per-route P50/P95/P99.
- alerting/kernel-sensitivity-p99-spike: triggers when KSI-based p99 delta > 150ms and traffic fraction > 5%.
- alerting/kernel-regression-ci-failure: flags if canary KSI exceeds +0.05 over three successive daily runs.

Guidance for release engineers
------------------------------
- Add KSI reports to the kernel candidate artifact in the release bundle under /artifacts/ksi/*.json.
- Require a KSI sign-off (responsible: perf-lead) for kernels with KSI > +0.02 on any production shape before global rollout.
- Use staged rollouts with weight 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with KSI checks at each gate.

Limitations and known caveats
----------------------------
- Small sample sizes for rare workload shapes inflate CI; prefer combining shapes with the same kernel hotpath.
- KSI attribution is sensitive to queueing effects; ensure queue depth tags are stable across A/B runs.
- Driver or compiler-level nondeterminism (JIT variability) can create noise — repeat runs and follow up with kernel-level deterministic tracing.

Maintenance and ownership
-------------------------
- Owner team: serving-runtime/perf (primary), eng-sre (secondary).
- Dashboard owner: telemetry-team.
- Review cadence: quarterly. Update this doc when the profiling agent or replay harness changes major versions (major semver).

Appendix: Quick checks and YAML example for CI gating
-----------------------------------------------------
YAML snippet (put into kernel-candidate CI job):

pipeline:
  steps:
    - name: run-ksi-smoke
      image: redwood/perf-tools:stable
      commands:
        - pytools/latency_fingerprint/compute_ksi.py --baseline baseline.json --candidate candidate.json --out ksi_report.json
        - if [ $(jq .ksi_value ksi_report.json) \u003e 0.02 ]; then echo "KSI exceeded"; exit 1; fi

If you have questions or need a dedicated pairing session to walk through the replay harness, ping the perf channel (#perf-runtime) or reach out to the doc reviewers listed above.
